which layers · order · stop-early · gate vs flag

svg.text: TYPE 2 — ADDITIONAL (adjusts / flags, up-only where noted)

svg.text: core rule: blocked/limited/broken → UNKNOWN, never invalid
principle: harden toward UNKNOWN, not valid/invalid

g.text: confidence earned only by clean 250 on non-catch-all
rule: trust their "no" a little, their "yes" never

svg.text: LOG record = response + verdict, joinable to bounce later

g.text: what you don't log now is gone forever
email hashing decided ONCE · never changes
disposable box: IP blocked → kill + spin fresh · no data lost (state in brain)

svg.text: ⑧ TOPOLOGY — same code, config only

g.text: reliability spend · holds all state · the "pet"

svg.text: 1. fork rack, pin gem, run unchanged · 2. LOG everything + /audit · 3. /verify wrapper (mock SMTP) · 4. catch-all probe · 5. disposable + config reload
6. cheap layers live (no port 25) · 7. real box + audit green → enable SMTP selectively · 8. router over node-list (N=1) · 9. scale by config
PARKED (seams exist): join table (needs sender) · queue · UI · platform-scraper tier · budget/circuit-breaker dropped (health-quarantine kept for IP protection)
Rule of thumb: anything that becomes historical data or that another system codes against is a one-way door. Everything else is a dial.
